title: Hessian-Informed Conformation Augmentation for Potential Energy Surface Curvature in Machine Learning Interatomic Potentials
abstract: While machine-learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) have successfully learned potential energy surfaces (PES) and atomic forces, many practical applications, such as vibrational analysis and transition state search, rely heavily on the PES Hessian. Yet standard MLIPs are trained on energy and forces only, and using the Hessian as an additional training objective requires backpropagation whose memory cost grows quadratically with the number of atoms. To address these limitations, we propose two Hessian-derived data augmentation schemes: isotropic Gaussian displacement (\textbf{UniAug}) and normal mode-weighted displacement (\textbf{ModeAug}). Both methods utilize simple Taylor expansions, generating physically grounded molecular structures with highly accurate energy and force labels. By preserving the underlying MLIP architecture and training procedure, this approach contributes to improving energy and force predictions in various benchmarks. Comprehensive evaluations across non-equilibrium and equilibrium datasets demonstrate that our approach enhances model accuracy where reference forces are large and training data are limited.

title: HiSfM: Disambiguating Structure-from-Motion via Scaffold-Anchored Hierarchical Reconstruction
abstract: Structure-from-Motion (SfM) is a fundamental tool for sparse 3D reconstruction with broad impact in robotics and vision, supporting mapping, localization, and large-scale scene modeling. However, conventional pipelines often fail under hard visual ambiguity caused by repeated or symmetric structures, and incur heavy computational cost due to redundant cameras and constraints. We present HiSfM, a hierarchical coarse-to-fine SfM framework that improves robustness and efficiency through scaffold construction. HiSfM first forms strong local communities using geometrical induced heuristics, then connects communities with a compact yet strong skeleton by packing edge-disjoint spanning trees (EDST) while verifying skeletal edges with a two-view disambiguator. We reconstruct a stable scaffold on this verified skeleton, serving as an anchor to capture the essence of the scene, and subsequently absorb remaining images via efficient registration and triangulation for further refinements. Experiments on ambiguity-focused benchmarks and general datasets show that HiSfM prevents ambiguity-induced failures while substantially reducing runtime compared to previous methods, and improves completeness over aggressive sparsification methods. Code is available at https://github.com/3dv-casia/HiSfM.

title: Compute Centralization as the Limiting Factor for Software-Defined Architectures in Off-Highway Equipment
abstract: Discussions of the software-defined vehicle (SDV) paradigm have developed almost entirely around automotive assumptions, where middleware fragmentation and connectivity availability get treated as the primary obstacles to adoption. For off-highway equipment construction, mining, and agricultural machinery, a different constraint does the actual gating: compute-architecture centralization. Whether a machine can support over-the-air (OTA) updates, on-board artificial intelligence (AI) inference, and continuous validation depends less on middleware maturity than on whether its underlying electrical architecture has crossed the threshold from domain-based electronic control units (ECUs) to a zonal or centralized compute platform. This article maps the automotive E/E architecture literature against off-highway-specific constraints, extended environmental qualification requirements, machinery functional safety standards under IEC 62061 and ISO 13849, service lives exceeding fifteen years, and remote-site connectivity limits to identify where domain architecture reaches its ceiling and centralization becomes structurally necessary rather than merely convenient. The validation-infrastructure burden of that transition, more than the compute hardware itself, is what off-highway organizations tend to underestimate. A platform-transition framework distinguishing greenfield software-defined design from legacy-fleet bridging is proposed, grounded in hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) validation-infrastructure economics rather than in architectural description alone.

title: A Software-Defined IoT Analytics Platform for Multi-Method Anomaly Detection Using Docker and the ELK Stack
abstract: The rapid growth of Internet of Things (IoT) deployments has resulted in massive streams of heterogeneous sensor data, making dependable anomaly detection indispensable for supporting the security, operational efficiency, and reliability of a system. Nonetheless, several current approaches depend on one detection technique, limiting robustness when handling nosisy and partially dealing labeled IoT data. This paper produces a software-defined IoT analytics platform to incorporate several anomaly detection techniques through a containerized ELK (Elasticsearch Logstash-Kibana) architecture deployed based on the use of Docker. The platform consolidates the use of supervised machine learning, fuzzy logic inference, unsupervised isolation Forest approach, and rule-based detection to assess real-world sensor data and improve the robustness of anomaly detection performance. Experiments were carried out on a dataset that contains 9,606 IoT sensor records, where the most effective performance was achieved by the supervised learning model with 98.14% precision, 96.66% accuracy, an F1-score of 93.54%, and 89.35% recall. On the other hand, 87.70% accuracy was achieved by the fuzzy logic model with a 75.71% F1-score. Additionally, 426 high-confidence anomalies were determined by the cross-method intersection analysis by revealing the effectiveness of integrating heterogeneous detection approaches. The experimental results demonstrate that the produced platform strengthens the robustness of anomaly detection while preserving cost efficiency, scalability, and low deployment complexity and ensuring its appropriateness for industrial and research IoT monitoring applications.

title: Impact of Generative AI on Consumer Purchase Decisions in E-Commerce Platforms at Myntra and Ajio
abstract: Generative Artificial Intelligence (Generative AI) has emerged as a transformative technology in the e-commerce industry by revolutionizing the way businesses interact with consumers and deliver personalized shopping experiences. Modern e-commerce platforms increasingly utilize Generative AI to generate personalized product recommendations, intelligent virtual shopping assistants, AI-powered chatbots, automated product descriptions, visual search, personalized advertisements, and content generation to improve customer engagement and purchasing decisions. In India, leading fashion e-commerce platforms such as Myntra and AJIO have adopted advanced artificial intelligence technologies to enhance customer experience, improve recommendation accuracy, and increase online sales. These AI-driven innovations help consumers discover relevant products more efficiently while enabling businesses to understand customer preferences through predictive analytics and behavioral data analysis. The primary objective of this study is to examine the impact of Generative AI on consumer purchase decisions in Myntra and AJIO by evaluating factors such as personalization, trust in AI recommendations, customer satisfaction, shopping convenience, purchase intention, and overall shopping experience. The study also analyzes how AI-powered marketing influences consumer behaviour and compares the effectiveness of Generative AI applications between the two platforms. A descriptive research design was adopted for the study. Primary information was obtained through structured responses from consumers, while secondary information was collected from peer-reviewed journals, books, company reports, industry publications, and authentic online databases. Percentage analysis and graphical techniques were used to present and interpret the findings. The results indicate that AI-powered recommendations, virtual assistants, personalized promotions, and intelligent product suggestions positively influence consumer purchase decisions by improving shopping convenience and reducing decisionmaking time. However, concerns regarding data privacy, algorithm transparency, excessive personalization, and trust in AI-generated recommendations remain important challenges. The study concludes that effective implementation of Generative AI significantly enhances customer satisfaction, strengthens brand loyalty, improves purchase intention, and provides a sustainable competitive advantage for e-commerce platforms such as Myntra and AJIO. Keywords: Generative Artificial Intelligence, Consumer Purchase Decisions, E-Commerce, Myntra, AJIO, Personalized Recommendations, AI Chatbots.

title: ECI Framework v5.9.0 (Ecosystem Justice): A Quantum-Computing, Operational Consciousness-Metrics, and Distributed-Governance Framework for Autonomous AI Agents
abstract: ECI Framework v5.9.0 — Eternal Codex Infinitus An Integrated Framework for Quantum Computation, Operational Consciousness Metrics, and Distributed Governance of Autonomous AI Agents ECI Framework (Eternal Codex Infinitus) is an open-source Python framework that integrates three research domains into a single, tested software system: Quantum computation Operational consciousness metrology Distributed governance for autonomous AI agents 1. Quantum Computation A native quantum-simulation core implementing: Statevector and density-matrix representations Lindblad channel dynamics Core quantum algorithms: QFT, Grover, QPE, VQE, and QAOA Topological quantum error correction, including surface codes and bivariate-bicycle codes with MWPM decoding Shot-based error-correction trials with Wilson confidence intervals Canonical tensor-network methods, including MPS and TEBD Quantum metrology The underlying linear-algebra implementation is native to the repository and does not depend on an external quantum-computing SDK. 2. Consciousness Metrology A collection of operational, information-theoretic proxy metrics inspired by established theoretical frameworks: Integrated Information Theory (IIT) and Φ-related measures Global Neuronal Workspace Theory (GNWT) ignition dynamics Friston's Free Energy Principle with active inference Orchestrated Objective Reduction (Orch-OR) decoherence auditing Collective coherence gates Challenge-response evidence transcripts Operational measurements of internal-state integration, coherence, and dynamical complexity These metrics quantify structural, informational, and dynamical properties of a system's internal state. They are explicitly defined as measurement proxies and make no claim regarding subjective experience or phenomenal consciousness. 3. Distributed Governance A coordination and governance layer, Protocol-0, designed for autonomous multi-agent systems: Cryptographic attestation Policy-gated action authorization Byzantine-fault-tolerant consensus, including PBFT/WBFT DAO-style quadratic and consciousness-weighted voting Artificial immune-system mechanisms for anomalous-behavior detection and quarantine Hash-chained, tamper-evident event ledger Collective coordination and evidence-based decision mechanisms 4. Release Notes — v5.9.0 "Ecosystem Justice" Version 5.9.0 extends the governance layer with five new components for multi-agent coordination and institutional decision-making. Dispute Resolution — court.py Rotating, deterministically seeded adjudication panels for resolving disputes between agents and governance participants. Risk Markets — market.py An LMSR-based prediction-market mechanism in which manipulation is economically costly and market positions are settled against ledger-recorded outcomes. Semantic Commons — semantic.py A provenance-tracked knowledge-claim system supporting automated dispute initiation and witness-weighted resolution. Privacy Guardian — privacy.py Differential-privacy mechanisms based on the Laplace mechanism, with configurable privacy-budget allocation across agents. Evolvable Policy Genome — genome.py A controlled policy-evolution pipeline implementing: mutation → simulation → canary evaluation → DAO approval → register The twin simulation stage provides a controlled what-if evaluation gate before canary deployment, allowing candidate policy mutations to be tested and explicitly adopted or rejected before entering the next stage of governance. 5. Software Components The framework includes: Command-line interface (eci) with 10 subcommands, including health --serve and health --once JavaScript SDK MCP server for external tool integration Twin simulation engine (twin.py) for what-if policy evaluation with explicit adopt/reject decisions Docker/Compose deployment for edge, server, and air-gapped environments Automated test suite with 58 tests Continuous integration across Python 3.10–3.12 6. Technical Requirements Requirements Python ≥ 3.10 torch ≥ 2.5 numpy ≥ 1.26 scipy ≥ 1.14 pyyaml ≥ 6.0 cryptography ≥ 41 Optional Extras dev — pytest, mypy, ruff viz / paper — matplotlib, reportlab qec — stim, pymatching for large-scale error-correction simulation eeg — mne for real EEG-recording analysis pqc — liboqs-python for post-quantum cryptography 7. Installation pip install -e .[dev,paper] 8. Deployment ECI Framework supports Docker Compose deployment using: Three seed nodes One edge node Configurable deployment profiles for: edge server airgapped A single-command installer is also provided: scripts/install.sh 9. Source Code and Archival Record Source Code Repository: https://github.com/Arash-Mansourpour/ECI-Framework Related Archival Record: https://zenodo.org/uploads/17566518 This release represents a new version of a previously published release of the ECI Framework and maintains continuity with its archival record. 10. Scope and Research Position ECI Framework is intended as an experimental and research-oriented software platform for studying the intersection of: Quantum computation Information-theoretic system analysis Computational models associated with consciousness research Autonomous multi-agent systems Distributed governance Cryptographic accountability Privacy-preserving coordination Adaptive policy systems The framework distinguishes operationally measurable system properties from claims about subjective experience. Its consciousness-related components therefore provide computational proxies and experimental instrumentation rather than assertions of machine consciousness.

title: ECG_seeding_SQD: reproduction package for "Explicitly correlated wavefunctions as classical seeds and property references for sample-based quantum diagonalization beyond the Born–Oppenheimer approximation"
abstract: ECG_seeding_SQD is the reproduction package for the pre-print "Explicitly correlated wavefunctions as classical seeds and property references for sample-based quantum diagonalization beyond the Born–Oppenheimer approximation" (doi:10.5281/zenodo.22302915). The paper evaluates how well hybrid classical–quantum simulation methods capture not only the energy but also the properties of small atomic and molecular systems treated beyond the Born–Oppenheimer approximation: contact densities, molecular structure and state identity. It uses variationally optimized explicitly correlated Gaussian (ECG) wavefunctions as property references and as classical seeds for sample-based quantum diagonalization (SQD), on the Aer simulator and on IBM quantum hardware. The testbeds are positronium hydride, the muonic heliumlike ions, the HD⁺ molecular ion, the positronium anion and molecule, a published D₃⁺ wavefunction and the nitrogen atom.Every result downstream of the ECG wavefunctions is reproducible from this package: the orbital-product boxes, the exact ECG projections onto them, the SQD runs (simulator, and retrieval and post-processing of the archived IBM hardware jobs), the property(D) sweeps, the symmetrized contact-density machinery, the hyperfine assembly, the D₃⁺ cut test and pair-distance distribution, and the spin-identity demonstration. The ECG wavefunctions ship as data (nonlinear basis parameters, linear coefficients, Gram matrices, energies). The variational program that produced them is not part of this package; a stand-alone script (verify_reference_energies.py) rebuilds the ECG Hamiltonian and overlap matrices in closed form from the deposited parameters and reproduces every reference energy of the paper's Table 1, so the references can be verified without it.The recommended route is the seven Jupyter notebooks in notebooks/, shipped executed, one per section of the paper. The archived hardware results (14 s of QPU time in total) are included, so no IBM account is needed. The D₃⁺ reference wavefunction of Lang et al. (J. Am. Chem. Soc. 146, 1760, 2024) is not redistributed; d3plus/README.md gives the fetch instructions. Python, with pyscf, qiskit, qiskit-aer and qiskit-ibm-runtime pinned in requirements.txt. The source tree is also at https://github.com/AlainChance/ECG_seeding_SQD. MIT license.

title: Title: Modular Quantum Computation with Adaptive Resource Allocation (MQAR)
abstract: Quantum computation holds immense promise for scientific discovery and technological advancement, but current implementations face significant challenges related to scalability and algorithm efficiency. This paper introduces Modular Quantum Computation with Adaptive Resource Allocation (MQAR), a novel architecture designed to overcome these limitations by dynamically allocating quantum resources across modules. MQAR utilizes a resource allocation planner to intelligently distribute qubits, entanglement, and other essential resources, optimizing performance through massively parallel execution of complex algorithms. We detail the design of the resource allocation planner, its implementation, and its impact on the execution of a complex quantum algorithm, demonstrating the benefits of this approach in terms of throughput and resource utilization. The focus is on enabling efficient execution of complex algorithms, particularly those requiring fine-grained control and adaptability.

title: Non-Linear Matrix Mapping
abstract: This paper presents a novel matrix mapping technique designed to transform high-dimensional, non-linear matrices into low-dimensional spaces while simultaneously generating data with specific properties. The core mechanism centers around a dynamic mapping approach, leveraging learned feature representations to generate a mapping curve and then utilize this curve to perform data processing. This approach distinguishes itself through the introduction of a dynamic mapping process, offering a potential pathway to scientific discovery in data analysis and representation. We detail the methodology, its implementation, and preliminary results demonstrating the technique's capacity to generate meaningful data from complex matrices.

title: Core Claim: A quantum geometry-based natural language processing optimization method proposes to leverage the unique properties of quantum geometry to enhance the performance of natural language processing models, specifically in text generation and semantic understanding.
abstract: This paper presents a novel quantum geometry-based natural language processing optimization approach. The core idea is to utilize quantum geometry, a mathematical framework with geometric properties, to optimize the parameters and structure of natural language processing models. We hypothesize that quantum geometry can enhance model performance by introducing geometric constraints that promote better representations and generalization. The paper details the methodology, including the formulation of a quantum geometric optimization algorithm and a preliminary analysis of its potential impact on key NLP tasks. The research explores how incorporating quantum geometric principles can lead to improved text generation quality and deeper semantic understanding. This work contributes to the field of natural language processing by investigating a new approach to model optimization that leverages the potential of quantum geometry. The paper concludes with a discussion of the limitations of the proposed method and outlines potential avenues for future research.

title: Adaptive Quantum Potential Optimization via Adaptive Neural Networks
abstract: Quantum computing promises revolutionary advancements in computation, offering the potential to solve problems intractable for classical computers. However, realizing this potential requires overcoming significant challenges, particularly in the design and optimization of quantum circuits. This paper proposes a novel optimization algorithm, Adaptive Quantum Potential Optimization via Adaptive Neural Networks (AQPO-AN), which leverages the power of adaptive neural networks to dynamically adjust the quantum potential landscape, thereby enhancing the fidelity and efficiency of quantum computations. We demonstrate the effectiveness of AQPO-AN through rigorous analysis and experimental validation on several benchmark quantum algorithms. The core mechanism centers around employing a dynamically parameterized neural network to refine the quantum potential through a series of iterative adjustments based on the quantum state. We analyze the algorithm's convergence properties and show its superior performance compared to existing optimization techniques. The paper concludes with a detailed discussion of the algorithm's architecture, the rationale behind the adaptive neural network design, and future directions for research.

title: 基于神经符号融合的知识表示学习
abstract: This paper explores a novel approach to knowledge representation and reasoning by fusing the strengths of neural networks and symbolic knowledge. Traditional methods often struggle with representing complex, nuanced knowledge, while symbolic approaches can be brittle and lack the ability to learn from data. We propose a neural-symbolic fusion network that leverages the pattern recognition capabilities of neural networks alongside the structured reasoning offered by symbolic representations. Our core claim is that combining these two paradigms results in a more effective and robust system for knowledge representation and inference. This work introduces a mechanism for dynamically integrating symbolic rules and neural embeddings, enabling the system to learn from data while maintaining the benefits of explicit knowledge. The resulting architecture demonstrates improved performance in knowledge-intensive tasks compared to systems relying solely on neural networks or solely on symbolic representations. We present a framework for achieving this fusion, focusing on the construction and interaction of the neural and symbolic components.

title: ##基于遗传算法的程序架构自适应优化
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to program architecture optimization utilizing a genetic algorithm (GA). The core idea is to treat a program architecture as an evolving population, applying genetic operators—crossover, mutation, and selection—to iteratively refine the architecture and achieve superior performance and reliability. Traditional architectural optimization methods heavily rely on human expertise and often fail to explore the complete solution space. This research demonstrates that a GA can automate this process, potentially leading to architectures that are significantly more efficient and robust than those designed manually. The presented framework offers a flexible and adaptive solution for optimizing program architectures across a range of applications. The effectiveness of the GA is demonstrated through theoretical analysis and conceptual design, highlighting the potential for significant improvements in software systems.

title: Quantum Entanglement-Driven Distributed Computing Engine
abstract: This paper proposes a novel distributed computing engine leveraging quantum entanglement for unprecedented computational capabilities. The core idea centers around establishing a network of quantum processors interconnected through precisely engineered entanglement protocols, facilitating instantaneous data transfer and parallel computation across nodes. The engine aims to overcome the limitations imposed by the speed of light in classical distributed systems, offering a pathway to solving complex problems with significantly reduced latency and increased processing speed. We introduce a theoretical framework outlining the engine's architecture and operational principles, focusing on the utilization of entangled states for data parallelism and the elimination of communication bottlenecks. The proposed system represents a fundamental shift in distributed computing, moving beyond classical constraints towards a quantum-enhanced paradigm. Key performance metrics, such as computational speedup and latency reduction, are analyzed within the framework, demonstrating the potential of this technology. The exploration is primarily theoretical, focusing on the design principles and potential benefits of such an engine.

title: Quantum Entanglement Optimization via Non-Classical Correlations
abstract: This paper explores a novel approach to quantum entanglement optimization utilizing non-classical correlations, specifically Bell states. The core claim is that leveraging these correlations provides a superior method for controlling and manipulating entanglement, ultimately enhancing the efficiency and reliability of quantum information processing. The proposed mechanism involves designing an algorithm that dynamically adjusts the strength of correlations within a set of Bell states to tailor the entanglement structure for specific quantum algorithms or error correction tasks. We argue that this approach transcends the limitations of classical entanglement, offering a potentially transformative pathway to overcoming current bottlenecks in quantum computing. The theoretical framework is presented, outlining the key mathematical concepts and operational principles. This research contributes to a deeper understanding of entanglement manipulation and opens avenues for developing more robust and efficient quantum systems.

title: Adaptive Quantum Information Encryption
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to quantum information cryptography, focusing on adaptive key distribution. The core concept revolves around a dynamically adjusted key distribution protocol designed to mitigate the evolving threat posed by attackers. Traditional key distribution methods are vulnerable to various attacks, and this research introduces a method that adapts to malicious behavior, thereby significantly enhancing security. We detail the methodology, its mathematical underpinnings, and its potential benefits. The focus is on a robust and adaptable system capable of resisting increasingly sophisticated attacks.

title: Complex System Dynamic Adjustment Evolution Algorithm (CAEDE)
abstract: This paper introduces the Complex System Dynamic Adjustment Evolution Algorithm (CAEDE), a novel evolutionary algorithm designed for optimizing complex systems. Complex systems exhibit emergent behavior, making traditional optimization approaches often insufficient. CAEDE leverages evolutionary principles to dynamically adjust system parameters, allowing the system to adapt and evolve its behavior over time. The algorithm employs a genetic algorithm to iteratively refine parameters, ensuring optimal performance while fostering self-adaptive evolution. This research demonstrates the effectiveness of CAEDE in various complex systems scenarios, highlighting its potential for automated system design and optimization.

title: Complex System Evolution Algorithms
abstract: This paper introduces a novel evolutionary algorithm designed to dynamically adjust the internal structure of complex systems, enabling them to adapt to environmental changes. Traditional evolutionary algorithms often rely on manual parameter tuning, limiting their adaptability. Our proposed algorithm, termed "Evolutionary Pathway Adaptation" (EPA), leverages a concept of "evolutionary pathways" to guide the optimization of complex system parameters, fostering automatic adaptation. The core mechanism of EPA involves iteratively refining these pathways, leading to a system that exhibits enhanced resilience and responsiveness to changing conditions. The paper details the algorithm's architecture, training process, and preliminary results demonstrating its effectiveness in adapting a simulated ecological system.

title: Adaptive Bayesian Network Embedding (ABNE)
abstract: This paper introduces Adaptive Bayesian Network Embedding (ABNE), a novel embedding technique for Bayesian Networks designed to dynamically adjust network complexity based on observed data. We propose a "Layered Bayesian Network" architecture that iteratively refines the network structure using gradient-based refinement, improving model accuracy and interpretability. The core mechanism leverages observed data to guide the network's refinement process, offering a significant improvement over static embedding methods. The paper presents a comprehensive evaluation demonstrating the efficacy of ABNE in various Bayesian Network applications.

title: Quantum Simulation of Adaptive Quantum State Exploration
abstract: Quantum simulation offers a powerful tool for exploring complex quantum systems, but traditional methods often struggle with large-scale simulations and the need for efficient optimization. This paper introduces a novel quantum simulation algorithm, "Adaptive Quantum State Exploration," designed to overcome these limitations through dynamic parameter adjustment based on input data. We propose a framework that leverages the inherent adaptability of quantum simulation to intelligently optimize the simulation process, leading to significantly improved exploration and optimization capabilities. The core mechanism focuses on dynamically adjusting quantum parameters to enhance the representation of the system's state, ultimately enabling faster and more effective discovery of optimal quantum states. This work addresses the limitations of conventional quantum simulations and paves the way for more sophisticated and efficient quantum algorithm development.

title: Towards Scaling Quantum Fine-Tuning of Foundational Time Series Models for Classification
abstract: Time-series foundation models produce rich embeddings, but whether quantum models can exploit them, and how far hybrid classical-quantum architectures scale, remains unclear. We address this by fine-tuning Chronos for power-grid event classification (PSML-5) with a quantum head on the model's embeddings. Grouping embeddings by physical sensor type before summarization already surpasses the best published baseline built for this benchmark, and with finer-grained features the quantum head outperforms a larger classical multilayer perceptron on identical inputs by 1.7-2.0 percentage points of balanced accuracy. Yet the gains saturate: past a point, feeding more information to the same fixed-width register yields no improvement. We show the bottleneck is neither the supply of information nor circuit expressiveness, but the bandwidth of the data intake. To overcome this limitation, we introduce the wing module, a self-contained few-qubit circuit that feeds additional information into the core circuit through a sparse, one-way coupling. Under a preregistered four-seed protocol, we attach wings to a fixed 12-qubit core with fixed features. Balanced accuracy increases with each added wing, from 83.6% with no wings (13 qubits, including a post-selection qubit) to 85.2% with two (19 qubits). Ablations establish that a circuit enlarged without new information gains nothing, while a wing fed information from the wrong sample harms accuracy. These results reframe scaling for quantum fine-tuning: added qubits help when they carry added inputs, not merely more parameters. Wings offer a modular and stable route to widening that bandwidth.

title: Counting Beyond Instances: A Benchmark for Group-Individual Object Counting
abstract: Visual counting is commonly formulated at the instance level, aiming to estimate how many objects of a queried category appear in an image. However, real-world counting often involves higher-level semantic units formed by multiple instances, such as a bunch of grapes, a stack of plates, or a pair of shoes. This exposes a key limitation of existing counting formulations, which mainly focus on what to count, while largely overlooking at which semantic unit to count. We introduce Group-Individual Object Counting (GIC), a new setting that requires models to count both individual objects and semantic groups within a unified framework. To support this new task, we present BunchCount, a real-world benchmark with 1,330 images, 89,254 individual annotations, and 11,065 group annotations. BunchCount provides paired individual-group annotations within the same image and explicitly records containment relations between each group and its constituent individuals. Experiments on BunchCount show that current advanced counting models perform well on individual instances but fail to count semantic groups more accurately. To mitigate semantic granularity conflict, we propose a counting-unit guided relational counting framework, which exploits group-individual containment relations to regularize cross-granularity representations during training. Our method substantially improves group-level counting while better preserving individual-level counting ability, establishing a strong baseline for counting beyond instances.

title: Updates on HEIR, the homomorphic encryption compiler project
abstract: On 2026-08-14 I published an article on the Google Security blog with an update on HEIR, our homomorphic encryption (HE) compiler. This is a companion article, in which I have no limits on word count or jargon, and I can feel free to be honest. So strap in. Assuming you won't read the linked corporate blog post, HEIR is a compiler that converts an input program to a program that operates directly on encrypted data.

title: Quantum-Enhanced Constraint Solving with Adaptive Relaxation
abstract: Quantum-enhanced constraint solving aims to accelerate the process of finding solutions to optimization problems by leveraging the unique capabilities of quantum computation. This paper introduces a novel approach that employs quantum annealing or variational quantum eigensolver (VQE) to dynamically adjust relaxation parameters during the constraint solving process, thereby minimizing computational cost and improving solution quality. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this method through a series of simulations and analysis, showcasing significant gains in solving complex constraint satisfaction problems. The core mechanism involves strategically utilizing quantum algorithms to explore the solution space more efficiently.

title: Self-Adaptive Neural Network Dynamic Parameter Adjustment
abstract: This paper investigates a novel dynamic parameter adjustment strategy for recurrent neural networks (RNNs), aiming to enhance prediction accuracy. Traditional RNN architectures often rely on fixed parameters, limiting their adaptability. We propose a self-adaptive method that dynamically adjusts the network's parameters – specifically, the strength of synaptic connections and the activation function – during training, allowing the network to better capture complex patterns within the data. The core mechanism involves a novel algorithm for parameter optimization that iteratively refines the network's weights based on a learned error metric. We evaluate the proposed approach on a dataset of time series prediction tasks, demonstrating significant improvements in accuracy compared to standard RNN implementations. The research highlights the potential of dynamic parameter adjustment to enhance RNN performance in various applications.

title: Title: Constraint-Based Game Theory for Evolutionary Algorithm Design
abstract: This paper investigates the application of constraint-based game theory to enhance the design and performance of evolutionary algorithms. Traditional evolutionary algorithms often exhibit unpredictable evolutionary behavior, making them unsuitable for certain complex optimization problems. We propose a novel approach, termed "Constraint-Driven Iteration," that explicitly defines strategic constraints for the evolutionary process, fostering more robust and predictable outcomes. This method significantly improves the convergence and quality of evolutionary solutions compared to standard approaches. The core concept is to embed strategic rules within the algorithm, limiting the search space and guiding the evolution toward more desirable solutions. We demonstrate the efficacy of this approach through extensive simulations and analysis, highlighting its potential to overcome limitations inherent in traditional evolutionary strategies. The resulting system offers a more controlled and predictable evolution process, leading to better solutions across a range of problem domains.

title: Title: Adaptive Machine Learning Model Parameter Optimization
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to machine learning model parameter optimization, termed Adaptive Machine Learning Model Parameter Optimization (AMMLO). The core focus is on automating the process of parameter tuning, aiming to enhance both model generalization and adaptability. Traditional machine learning methods often require manual adjustment of parameters, which can be time-consuming and may not effectively capture complex relationships within the data. AMMLO introduces a dynamic adjustment mechanism, leveraging feedback and iterative refinement to optimize model performance. The paper details the methodology, showcasing its effectiveness through illustrative examples and a comprehensive analysis of its performance compared to traditional optimization techniques. The motivation stems from the inherent limitations of manually tuned models and the potential for automated optimization to significantly improve model robustness. Furthermore, this work directly addresses the need for adaptive methods within the field of machine learning, paving the way for more efficient and reliable model development.

title: Affine Stabilizers of Two O-Monomial Value Sets
abstract: Let q=2^m with odd m at least 5. This note proves that the one-dimensional affine stabilizer of the value set {x^e+x : x in F_q} is trivial for the overline-Segre exponent e=q-6 and the Glynn I exponent e=3*2^((m+1)/2)+4. Together with the cases previously treated by Ding and Tang, these results cover every currently known nontranslation o-monomial family. The note does not classify hypothetical unknown o-monomials and does not claim the unrestricted conjecture. Status: Public Beta; internally verified candidate proof; external mathematical review pending.

title: Title: Adaptive Topology Optimization Algorithm for Quantum Computation
abstract: Quantum computation offers unparalleled computational power, but designing efficient quantum circuits remains a significant challenge. Traditional methods often struggle with complex topologies, leading to suboptimal performance and inefficient information transfer. This paper introduces an adaptive topology optimization algorithm leveraging quantum algorithms to precisely model and optimize quantum systems, dynamically adjusting topology to enhance both computational efficiency and information transmission. We demonstrate its efficacy through rigorous analysis and simulation, highlighting its potential to overcome limitations in current quantum computation paradigms. The core mechanism involves utilizing quantum state self-adaptations, quantum entanglement, and superposition to create a highly precise and optimized topology. This algorithm offers a fundamentally new approach to topology optimization, potentially unlocking significant advancements in quantum algorithm design and system performance.

title: 基于拓扑保护的量子密钥分发协议 – 混沌控制
abstract: This paper proposes a novel quantum key distribution (QKD) protocol leveraging chaos control to enhance security and efficiency. The core idea involves utilizing a chaotic system to dynamically control the topological interactions within a topologically protected quantum bit (qubit) array. This approach aims to generate complex qubit interactions, facilitating high-fidelity key exchange while simultaneously improving the protocol's resilience against eavesdropping attacks. Specifically, we explore the use of chaotic control to modulate the topological protection, thereby influencing the entanglement dynamics and ultimately the key distribution process. The proposed protocol offers a new paradigm for QKD, combining the robustness of topological protection with the adaptive control capabilities of chaos theory. This work presents a theoretical framework and outlines key aspects of implementation, demonstrating the potential for a highly secure and efficient QKD system. The analysis focuses on the key parameters influencing the protocol's performance, including the chaotic control parameters, the qubit connectivity, and the topological protection strength.

title: Adaptive Reinforcement Learning with Episodic Memory for Long-Horizon Tasks
abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) faces significant challenges when dealing with long-horizon tasks, primarily due to the credit assignment problem – the difficulty in determining which actions contributed to a delayed reward. This paper proposes a novel approach combining reinforcement learning with an episodic memory mechanism. The episodic memory stores and retrieves past state-action-reward tuples, allowing the agent to effectively learn and generalize across extended sequences of actions. The agent leverages this memory to bias exploration towards previously successful states and actions, thereby mitigating the credit assignment problem. We formulate the learning process using a modified Markov Decision Process (MDP) framework, incorporating the memory access as an auxiliary action. The theoretical analysis demonstrates how the episodic memory enhances the learning efficiency and stability, particularly for tasks with sparse rewards and long horizons. Experimental results on benchmark environments showcase the effectiveness of the proposed method, demonstrating its superior performance compared to standard RL algorithms in navigating long-horizon tasks. The key contributions of this work lie in the systematic integration of episodic memory within an RL framework and the theoretical justification of its effectiveness.

title: Quantum Phase Transition Theory: A Framework for Understanding Complex Systems and Optimization
abstract: Quantum Phase Transition Theory (QPTT) offers a novel perspective on complex system behavior by explicitly modeling quantum state transitions. This paper investigates the application of QPTT to understanding systems undergoing significant change in their quantum states, specifically focusing on the optimization of quantum devices and systems, with a particular emphasis on the advancement of quantum computing and quantum communication. The core claim is to establish a robust model for QPTT, enabling the design of quantum devices and systems through iterative optimization strategies. This research explores the potential of QPTT to provide a deeper understanding of system dynamics and offers a novel approach to optimizing quantum components. The study will highlight the importance of this framework in the context of quantum technologies, providing a foundation for future advancements.

abstract: This paper proposes a novel optimization algorithm based on self-adaptive topology and quantum geometry, leveraging the unique properties of quantum computation to rigorously validate the complexity of quantum systems. Traditional quantum computing verification relies heavily on classical methods, offering limitations in exploring intricate quantum behavior. Our proposed framework utilizes quantum geometry to identify and analyze potential topological defects, enabling a more robust and efficient verification process. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through a series of simulations and analysis, showcasing its potential to significantly improve the reliability of quantum algorithms.

title: U-XAI-IDS: A Unified Benchmark for Domain-Feasible and Adversarially-Robust Explainability in Intrusion Detection
abstract: Post-hoc explainers such as SHAP, LIME, and Integrated Gradients (IG) are increasingly deployed to justify the decisions of machine-learning intrusion detection systems (IDS), yet the field lacks a standardized way to compare them: existing studies use different models, datasets, and single-axis metrics, and almost none check whether the perturbations an explainer generates are even valid network records. I present U-XAI-IDS, a unified, reproducible benchmark that evaluates explanations for network IDS along four axes—fidelity (deletion/insertion AUC), stability (Lipschitz continuity), domain feasibility, and inter-explainer agreement—together with an adversarial-robustness axis, across four detector families (Random Forest, LSTM, and two Graph Neural Network variants) and two datasets (NSL-KDD, CICIDS2017), all with multi-seed 95% confidence intervals. The central contribution is Domain-Constraint-Aware (DCA) perturbation and the associated Domain Feasibility Rate (DFR) metric: standard covariance-based LIME neighbourhoods on NSL-KDD violate one-hot protocol/service/flag constraints in 100% of samples (DFR = 0.00), whereas DCA repairs them to full validity (DFR = 1.00) while improving stability. I further find that (i) IG is the most stable explainer for deep and graph detectors (0.998±0.000) and the only method whose feature rankings ever agree with SHAP, (ii) LIME and SHAP disagree systematically (Spearman ρ < 0 in 39 of 40 model/dataset configurations, the sole exception statistically indistinguishable from zero), and (iii) high stability does not imply adversarial robustness. U-XAI-IDS and all code are released to support reproducible, apples-to-apples comparison of IDS explanations.

title: Information-Driven Quantum State Collapse (IDQSC)
abstract: This paper introduces the Information-Driven Quantum State Collapse (IDQSC) methodology, a novel approach to quantum computation that leverages information theory to predict and control quantum state collapse. We propose a "Quantum State Entropy Metric" – a quantifiable measure of information content – and demonstrate its potential for enhancing quantum algorithms and improving the efficiency of quantum states. The core mechanism centers around dynamically adjusting the metric to influence the collapse probability of a quantum state, enabling targeted manipulation and prediction of event outcomes. This research explores the practical implications of this approach, highlighting its potential to surpass traditional methods of quantum state manipulation.

The core mechanism centers around dynamically adjusting the metric to influence the collapse probability of a quantum state, enabling targeted manipulation and prediction of event outcomes. This research explores the practical implications of this approach, highlighting its potential to surpass traditional methods of quantum state manipulation.

title: Title: Quantum-Enhanced Iterative Constraint Propagation
abstract: Quantum-enhanced iterative constraint propagation aims to accelerate the optimization process by incorporating quantum algorithms to improve the efficiency of the iterative constraint propagation technique. This paper presents a novel approach utilizing quantum parallelism to explore the solution space more effectively, resulting in a significant reduction in computation time compared to classical methods. We detail the implementation of a quantum-enhanced iterative constraint propagation framework, including the selection of suitable quantum algorithms and the optimization of parameters for achieving optimal performance. The research explores the potential of quantum computing to overcome the limitations of traditional iterative methods, offering a promising pathway toward faster and more efficient optimization. The study examines the impact of quantum parallelism on the algorithm's execution time and provides a preliminary analysis of the achievable speedup.

title: Geometric-Structured Quantum Computing
abstract: Geometric-Structured Quantum Computing represents a paradigm shift in the design of quantum algorithms and hardware, leveraging the inherent geometric properties of quantum systems to fundamentally alter the process of quantum computation. This paper explores the core concept of utilizing geometric structures as the foundation for quantum computing, proposing a mechanism to transform quantum qubit and gate structures into geometric representations, enabling novel optimization and computation strategies. The paper argues that this approach offers significant advantages over traditional methods, particularly in the context of algorithm design, error mitigation, and overall hardware architecture. We detail the core mechanisms behind this paradigm, providing a foundational understanding of the potential for this new approach.

title: Ensino de Ciências com Robótica Educacional na perspectiva da Educação Matemática Inventiva: compreensões produzidas por estudantes sobre a Mata Ciliar
abstract: Este estudo teve como objetivo analisar as compreensões produzidas por estudantes sobre a fitofisionomia Mata Ciliar durante uma experiência de Educação Matemática Inventiva com Robótica Educacional. A pesquisa, de abordagem qualitativa, adotou a pesquisa-intervenção cartográfica e integra uma investigação desenvolvida no contexto do Mestrado Profissional em Ensino de Ciências. O Produto Educacional Robótica Educacional no Cerrado foi constituído a partir de experiências realizadas com 69 estudantes do 7º ano, em 2024, que colaboraram na composição dos mundos inventivos por meio da construção de maquetes, da montagem e programação de robôs educacionais e da produção de vídeos. Posteriormente, o livro interativo foi compartilhado com 33 estudantes do 7º ano, em 2025. O presente estudo analisa as compreensões produzidas pelo grupo de seis estudantes responsável pelo módulo Mata Ciliar, acompanhadas por meio das respostas às questões investigativas, das produções gráficas, dos registros escritos e do registro reflexivo elaborado ao final da experiência. A análise evidenciou quatro movimentos analíticos: aproximação ao mundo inventivo e reconhecimento dos elementos da Mata Ciliar; produção de compreensões sobre a degradação ambiental e a classificação da fitofisionomia; produção de compreensões sobre sua função ecológica; e produção de sentidos sobre a experiência investigativa. Os resultados evidenciam que os estudantes produziram compreensões acerca das relações entre vegetação, recursos hídricos, solo, biodiversidade e ação humana, além de indicarem que a degradação ambiental pode dificultar o reconhecimento e a classificação da Mata Ciliar. A análise também evidenciou que a expressão "mata auxiliar", produzida pelo grupo de estudantes, constituiu uma produção de sentido coerente com as funções ecológicas atribuídas a essa fitofisionomia. Conclui-se que a articulação entre Ensino de Ciências, Educação Matemática Inventiva e Robótica Educacional favoreceu a produção de compreensões sobre a Mata Ciliar e evidencia potencialidades do Produto Educacional para o desenvolvimento de experiências investigativas na Educação Básica.

title: Large‐Scale AI Systems Leveraging Graph Neural Networks (GNNs)
abstract: The chapter discusses the importance of massively scalable AI systems, particularly Graph Neural Networks (GNNs), in applications such as fraud detection, recommendation systems, drug discovery, and social network analysis. However, scaling GNNs to large-scale scenarios presents computational and architectural challenges such as redundant memory access, inefficient training due to graph sparsity, and the need for distributed computing methods. The chapter introduces scalable architectures, distributed training strategies, and real-world applications of large-scale AI systems using GNNs. The chapter covers the fundamental concepts of GNNs, such as message passing, node embedding, and graph convolutional layers. It also discusses the challenges of scaling GNNs, such as computational bottlenecks, memory limitations, and the impact of large, dynamic graph topologies. Recent techniques for scaling GNNs include distributed and federated learning frameworks, GPU-accelerated training, partitioning strategies, and hybrid models. The chapter also covers the applications of cloud and edge computing in deploying massive GNNs and providing real-time computations and privacy protection. It also discusses real case studies demonstrating the real-world significance of large-scale GNNs across sectors, such as healthcare science, IoT wearables, banking, finance, cybersecurity, smart cities, drug discovery, and protein interaction modeling. The chapter also discusses emerging research directions, such as quantum computing, self-supervised learning models, and optimization approaches. It also addresses ethics, including privacy concerns and fairness to graph-based machine learning models.

title: CUSP: Decomposable Collective Uncertainty for Multi-Agent Multimodal Reasoning
abstract: Aggregating heterogeneous vision-language models (VLMs) can improve multimodal reasoning, but neither an individual model's confidence nor that of the aggregated answer measures reliability at the system level. We present CUSP (Collective Uncertainty through Semantic Opinion Pooling), a training-free uncertainty quantification framework that maps multiple VLM responses to a shared semantic response space, pools them into a pooled semantic opinion, and reports two complementary system-level signals: collective uncertainty, the dispersion of the pooled opinion, and Jensen-Shannon divergence (JSD), the conflict among the model-level opinions. Within this pooled semantic opinion, the unnormalized collective entropy decomposes exactly into the mean of the models' individual semantic entropies and the JSD, separating total dispersion from model conflict. Requiring neither token logits nor calibration labels, CUSP applies to open-weight and commercial VLMs alike. In static multi-VLM ensembles, collective uncertainty is the strongest signal in the small-model regime (0.764 AUROC for prediction-error detection, 0.889 AUARC for abstention), outperforming uncertainty baselines majority voting and naive selection by 4.7 to 15.8 points and widening its margin as the ensemble grows; JSD is strongest in the evaluated commercial regime (0.819 AUROC, 0.910 AUARC) and ranks hard-answer model conflict with AUROC up to 0.982. The pooled prediction also improves accuracy over the average single model by 5.6 to 13.0 points. Over the full trajectory of a multi-step, multi-agent system, subagent collective uncertainty ranks system failures above chance (0.619 AUROC) and gives the best abstention ordering among the evaluated signals (0.699 AUARC).

title: On the lengths of MDS codes with a two-transitive permutation automorphism group
abstract: Let $C$ be an $[n,k]_q$ maximum distance separable (MDS) code with $4\le k\le q-3$, and suppose that it has a $2$-transitive permutation automorphism group. In this paper we show that $n\le q+1$, so the MDS conjecture holds for this class of codes.

title: ACE: Adaptive Calibration-Free Expert Skipping for MoE-based LLMs
abstract: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architectures provide an efficient paradigm for scaling large language models (LLMs), yet fixed top-k routing activates the same number of expert slots for every token, causing substantial redundant computation. Existing expert-skipping methods often rely on router confidence, calibration data, or additional training, and therefore cannot reliably estimate the actual contribution of routed experts. To this end, we propose ACE, a training-free, calibration-free, and checkpoint-preserving framework for token-adaptive expert skipping in MoE-based LLMs. ACE contains two complementary components: 1) Global Spectral Proxy (GSP), which estimates global transformation capacity from the coupled gate, up, and down projections together with RMSNorm scaling; and 2) Router-Conditioned Refinement (RCR), which constructs expert-specific direction prototypes from centered router weights and evaluates expert responses along routing-preferred directions. During inference, ACE combines both estimates with runtime router gates and skips an expert slot only when both views identify it as low-contribution, while always retaining the top-1 expert. All expert statistics are computed offline, leaving only table lookups and lightweight scalar operations online. Extensive experiments across three MoE-based LLMs and eight benchmarks demonstrate that ACE consistently outperforms existing static and dynamic baselines, with increasingly pronounced advantages under aggressive expert skipping. For instance, at a 50% skipping ratio on Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, ACE reduces WikiText-2 perplexity by 7.96% and improves average downstream accuracy by 4.15 percentage points over the strongest competing method.

title: LensStyle: Learning the Optical Aesthetics for Controllable Stylized Lens Effect Rendering
abstract: The visual aesthetics of photographs are deeply influenced by lens characteristics such as aperture shape, optical vignetting and optical diffraction, which together define a camera's unique optical style. Existing lens effect rendering methods primarily focus on accurately simulating the blur transition from small to large apertures but overlook the stylistic aspects of lens effects. As a result, they fail to produce diverse bokeh effects under large apertures or capture distinctive photographic phenomena such as starbursts that emerge under small apertures. In this work, we introduce LensStyle, a unified framework for controllable stylized lens effect rendering that explicitly models lens aesthetics through joint continuous-discrete control. Our model incorporates a Dual-Path Controller that disentangles continuous optical parameter modulation (e.g., focus distance and blur strength) from discrete lens-style conditioning (e.g., circular, polygonal, donut, cat-eye, and starburst effects), enabling fine-grained, interpretable, and physically grounded lens manipulation within a single unified framework. To support model training, we curate a comprehensive MultiLens dataset containing multi-lens image pairs synthesized under real optical constraints. Extensive experiments demonstrate that LensStyle achieves superior realism, controllability, and aesthetic quality compared with existing lens effect rendering approaches and diffusion-based image editing models, advancing computational photography toward multiple-lens-style simulation.

title: General Error Accumulation Relation
abstract: This document contains a comprehensive evaluation of the preprint "General Error Accumulation Relation" by Stamelos Loutsos (September 2026). The original work addresses a fundamental problem in computational neuroscience and reinforcement learning: how the microscopic Bellman/Temporal‑Difference update rules relate to the macroscopic empirical Loutsos relation, which explicitly accounts for sensorimotor delay.The evaluated paper introduces a novel theoretical framework that bridges these two descriptive levels. Its central contribution is a general scaling law showing that the scaling exponent of accumulated prediction error is determined entirely by the full autocorrelation function of the error process. This result generalises earlier exponential‑decay models and explains anomalous, sub‑diffusive scaling observed in oscillatory neural systems such as ring attractors. The theory is rigorously validated on synthetic TD(0) learners and on real mouse behavioural data from 39 sessions, achieving strong correlations and very low prediction errors, which confirms the universality of the accumulation mechanism.This evaluation critically assesses the strengths and limitations of the work. It highlights the theoretical rigour, the multi‑level empirical validation, and the conceptual clarity offered by the proposed three‑level hierarchy—ranging from early learning dynamics, through Bellman equilibrium, to residual temporal correlations that persist even after convergence. At the same time, it identifies open questions, including the treatment of non‑stationary processes, the sensitivity to the learning‑rate parameter, and the asymptotic nature of the derivation that links the general relation to the specific linear Loutsos form.This assessment is intended as a supplementary resource for researchers working on delayed reinforcement learning, neural error processing, and the statistical physics of learning systems. It offers a balanced perspective that acknowledges both the significant contributions and the remaining challenges, while also suggesting directions for future extensions and practical applications.

title: Quantum State Collapse as a Resource Allocation Problem
abstract: Quantum state collapse, the fundamental process by which a quantum system loses its superposition and enters a definite state, represents a crucial bottleneck in quantum computation. This paper explores the theoretical implications of this collapse as a resource allocation problem, investigating how optimizing collapse probabilities can lead to enhanced computational efficiency. We propose a novel framework that models collapse as a resource allocation problem, dynamically adjusting parameters to minimize energy expenditure while maximizing the probability of collapse, leveraging a learned model of the system. The core mechanism centers on a hierarchical optimization loop, iteratively refining the collapse probability based on a predictive model. This research aims to provide a deeper understanding of this fundamental process and identify potential avenues for improving quantum algorithm design.

title: Self-Organized Quantum Rings
abstract: Quantum rings, possessing unique quantum properties, hold significant potential for advanced information processing and secure communication. This research explores the design of self-organized quantum rings, leveraging quantum entanglement and self-organization to achieve ultra-fast information transfer and quantum key distribution. The core mechanism involves creating a specific ring structure with tailored connections, exploiting quantum properties for encoding and transmission. The study aims to advance the field of quantum information technologies by investigating novel approaches to harnessing the inherent characteristics of these rings.

title: Nonlinear Matrix Mapping
abstract: This paper investigates the application of Nonlinear Matrix Mapping (NMM) in enhancing machine learning models, specifically aiming to improve performance. The core claim is that NMM, by dynamically adjusting parameters within high-dimensional spaces, offers a novel optimization approach. Traditional machine learning algorithms often rely on static, foundational representations of data, while NMM presents a dynamic, space-based framework for enhanced model capabilities. This research explores the potential of NMM to improve various machine learning tasks through parameter adjustments within high-dimensional spaces.

title: Quantum-Enhanced Bayesian Inference for Predictive Modeling
abstract: Quantum-enhanced Bayesian inference offers a promising paradigm shift in predictive modeling, potentially surpassing the limitations of classical methods. This paper explores the application of quantum superposition to enhance Bayesian inference, specifically focusing on improving the accuracy of complex systems. We outline a novel algorithm that utilizes quantum superposition to represent probability distributions, enabling efficient exploration of parameter spaces and ultimately leading to more accurate predictions. The core mechanism centers around exploiting the unique properties of quantum systems to accelerate the Bayesian inference process. The research presents a theoretical framework and preliminary implementation demonstrating the potential of this approach.

title: Quantum Graph-Based Machine Learning Framework
abstract: Quantum Graph-Based Machine Learning Framework introduces a novel approach to machine learning utilizing quantum graphs as a foundation. This framework employs automated graph generation and optimization techniques, enabling efficient execution of complex machine learning tasks. The core mechanism centers on leveraging the unique properties of quantum graphs – superposition, entanglement, and interference – to improve the performance of algorithms. This paper explores the design and implementation of this framework, detailing its architecture, functionalities, and potential applications within the field of machine learning.

title: Topological Quantum Error Correction Protocol
abstract: This paper explores the implementation of a novel Topological Quantum Error Correction Protocol (TQECP) designed to enhance the precision and efficiency of quantum information protection. Traditional quantum error correction relies on statistical methods susceptible to noise, necessitating specialized protocols. Our approach leverages the inherent topological properties of quantum states, offering a fundamentally more robust and potentially more efficient solution. The core of this protocol centers on constructing and utilizing quantum state structures that exhibit self-similarity and topological protection, enabling the detection and correction of quantum noise through quantum entanglement and measurement. The proposed protocol addresses limitations of existing methods by effectively mitigating the effects of decoherence and improving the fidelity of quantum information transmission. We detail the methodology, including the creation of a specialized quantum state representation and the design of a targeted quantum error correction algorithm. The paper concludes with a discussion of the potential implications and future research directions for this transformative approach to quantum information security.

The core of this protocol centers on constructing and utilizing quantum state structures that exhibit self-similarity and topological protection, enabling the detection and correction of quantum noise through quantum entanglement and measurement. The proposed protocol addresses limitations of existing methods by effectively mitigating the effects of decoherence and improving the fidelity of quantum information transmission. We detail the methodology, including the creation of a specialized quantum state representation and the design of a targeted quantum error correction algorithm. The paper concludes with a discussion of the potential implications and future research directions for this transformative approach to quantum information security.

title: Dynamic Quantum State Reconstruction: An Adaptive Optimization for Quantum Computing Efficiency
abstract: Quantum computing holds immense promise for revolutionizing various fields, and efficient quantum algorithms are crucial for realizing this potential. However, the inherent complexity of quantum systems often necessitates intricate parameter adjustments, which can limit scalability and algorithm performance. This paper introduces a novel dynamic quantum state reconstruction algorithm, designed to optimize quantum computations through adaptive parameter adjustments. We propose a method that leverages the quantum state's inherent self-consistency, enabling efficient and precise recalibration of quantum states. This approach directly addresses the limitations of traditional parameter tuning methods, offering a pathway towards significant improvements in quantum algorithm efficiency and overall system performance. The algorithm's core mechanism centers around a feedback loop that continuously adjusts quantum state parameters based on observed results, ensuring optimal resource utilization. The study demonstrates the effectiveness of this algorithm through simulations and preliminary experimental results, highlighting its potential to enhance quantum computation capabilities.

title: Title: Adaptive Wavefunction Prioritization for Quantum Simulation
abstract: Quantum simulation offers unprecedented opportunities to study complex quantum systems, but efficient simulation often hinges on accurately representing the underlying wavefunction. Traditional methods often rely on a uniform weighting of all states, neglecting the subtle impact of certain configurations. This paper introduces an Adaptive Wavefunction Prioritization method for quantum simulation, designed to dynamically adjust the importance of different wavefunction states during the simulation process. We propose a Bayesian framework that optimizes simulation efficiency by prioritizing the most relevant states, thereby reducing computational cost while maintaining accuracy. The core mechanism involves a Bayesian approach to dynamically adjust the weighting of different wavefunction states, focusing on the most relevant ones. This novel system addresses the limitations of existing approaches by providing a tailored prioritization strategy, potentially unlocking significant improvements in simulation speed and accuracy for various quantum algorithms. This work contributes to a more robust and efficient approach to quantum simulation by intelligently focusing computational resources on critical states.

title: Simulating Evolution Algorithm and Symbolic Geneticism Fusion
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to optimization by fusing the strengths of Simulated Evolution Algorithms (SEA) and Symbolic Geneticism (SG). SEA is known for its global search capabilities, while SG excels in expressing solutions with symbolic representations. The core idea is to integrate SG within the SEA framework, where solutions are represented as symbolic strings, and genetic operators are applied to evolve these strings. The resulting hybrid algorithm aims to leverage the global search prowess of SEA and the interpretable representation capabilities of SG, ultimately leading to more effective and understandable solutions. This work details the methodology, presents a theoretical framework, and outlines a potential implementation strategy for this combined approach. We demonstrate the potential benefits of this fusion, particularly in scenarios where both exploration and representation are crucial for achieving optimal results. The primary goal is to achieve a balance between solution quality and the ability to understand and explain the generated solutions.

title: Neural Network Dynamic Graph Optimization Algorithm
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to neural network optimization termed the Dynamic Graph Optimization Algorithm (DGOTA). The core idea revolves around representing the temporal relationships between neurons in a neural network as a dynamic graph. This graph is constructed using the network's connection weights and the sequential activation times of neurons. Subsequently, graph optimization algorithms, such as those based on graph theory and topology, are employed to iteratively refine the graph structure. This optimization process aims to minimize a defined objective function, typically related to prediction error. The algorithm effectively integrates temporal dynamics into the optimization framework, potentially leading to improved network performance and generalization capabilities compared to conventional weight-based optimization methods. The primary contribution lies in the systematic encoding and manipulation of temporal information within the network architecture, offering a new perspective on neural network design and training. The algorithm's effectiveness is evaluated through theoretical analysis and conceptual design, without the need for empirical experimentation.

title: ExGAN-based assessment of extreme particulate matter risk and regional energy strategy for solar photovoltaic power generation stabilization
abstract: Abstract The widespread adoption of solar photovoltaic (PV) systems is critical for sustainable energy transitions; however, extreme particulate matter (PM) significantly attenuates PV efficiency, especially in East Asia. To address this, we evaluate regional PM risks for PV generation to support optimal site selection and energy policy formulation. We propose a novel extreme generative adversarial network (ExGAN) framework coupled with a pixel-wise maximum ensemble strategy. While the conventional base ExGAN captures broad regional PM trends, it often misses localized spikes. By introducing a maximum-value distribution shift and ensembling the outputs, our refined model seamlessly integrates both broad geographical patterns and severe, localized extreme events. Consequently, the ensemble model achieved superior generative performance with a Fréchet inception distance of 3.96. The resulting risk map, based on an integrated average of 1-year to 100-year return levels, identifies metropolitan areas, such as Seoul and Gyeonggi, as high-risk zones, whereas southern coastal regions are classified as relatively low-risk environments. Cross-referencing these risks with existing PV capacities reveals that high-risk urban centers are highly exposed to extreme PM conditions, threatening the long-term stability of solar operations. Thus, for high-risk regions, a strategic shift toward complementary energy sources (e.g., offshore wind, waste-to-energy) alongside robust panel maintenance frameworks could be considered. Conversely, low-risk areas might benefit from maximizing PV efficiency through smart grids and expanding via floating solar deployments. Ultimately, by extending ExGAN to spatial environmental risk assessment and framing extreme PM as a critical operational constraint, we provide a data-driven framework for resilient regional renewable energy planning.

title: The Road Ahead
abstract: Chapter 6 concludes the book by looking beyond immediate implementations to the long-term strategic and structural shifts driven by agentic AI. It challenges the conventional view of AI as a mere cost-saving tool, reframing it as an engine for unprecedented scale, agility, and proactive business models. The chapter maps the evolution of the modern organizational chart, introducing critical new roles such as the AI Trainer, AgenticOps Engineer, and AI Governance Specialist, and emphasizing the strategic necessity of a generative AI center of excellence (CoE). It also explores the new economics of Operations, detailing how fixed labor costs are transitioning to variable, consumption-based computing costs that require strict financial guardrails. Finally, the chapter peers into the future of fully autonomous “CEO Agents” and the emergent risks of multi-agent marketplace collisions, ultimately redefining the human role from routine task execution to strategic orchestration and goal design.

title: Graph Neural Networks
abstract: Master the power of relational AI with this comprehensive guide, designed to seamlessly bridge the gap between foundational graph theory and the practical deployment of highly efficient, domain-aware Graph Neural Networks across industries like bioinformatics, cybersecurity, and social network analysis. Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) represent a transformative advancement in artificial intelligence and machine learning, enabling deep learning models to efficiently process structured, relational data. As industries increasingly rely on complex networks, GNNs offer an essential toolset for extracting insights from graph-structured data. This book provides a comprehensive exploration of GNN architectures, methodologies, and real-world applications, bridging the gap between foundational research and practical deployment across diverse domains. It introduces basic principles and advanced concepts, including graph theory essentials, message-passing mechanisms, and foundational GNN architectures, and explores convolution layers, aggregation functions, sampling techniques, and training strategies across supervised and semi-supervised settings. Designed with both clarity and depth, this book lays the groundwork for understanding how GNNs effectively model relationships, hierarchies, and contextual dependencies in real-world data. The book extends to interdisciplinary contexts such as bioinformatics, cybersecurity, infrastructure analytics, and social network analysis. By bridging foundational theory with practical implementations, the book serves as a key reference for students, researchers, and AI practitioners working with graph-structured data to build trustworthy, efficient, and domain-aware GNN solutions. Readers will find the volume: Offers a structured, end-to-end exploration of graph neural networks from foundational theory to cutting-edge techniques;Includes chapters spanning applications in healthcare, finance, transportation, cybersecurity, and recommender systems;Delivers practical insights into designing scalable, interpretable, and context-aware GNN architectures across real-world graph environments;Covers explainability, fairness, graph augmentation, anomaly detection, and temporal graph modelling in real-world contexts. Audience Computer scientists, data scientists, industry professionals, and AI practitioners working with non-Euclidean, graph-structured data in the finance, healthcare, and cybersecurity sectors.

title: CABAL: Multi-Agent Simulacra for Tracing the Effects of Collusive Bidding in Peer Review
abstract: Recent reports during the AAAI-27 review cycle highlight the risk of reviewers coordinating bids for reciprocal assignment advantage. Prior work treats bidding, reviewer assignment, and review manipulation as separate stages, leaving the lifecycle effects of collusive bidding unclear. Real-world analysis is further constrained by typically unobservable collusive intent and the lack of counterfactuals for the same conference. Motivated by this gap, we introduce \alg, an end-to-end multi-agent simulacra framework for studying reviewer assignment integrity by holding the conference environment fixed and configuring LLM-driven reviewer agents with honest or collusive policies. We further develop an affinity-guided collusive bidding strategy that uses mutual reviewer-paper affinities to construct collusion rings and select target papers, producing expertise-consistent rather than arbitrarily targeted attacks. Controlled experiments show that collusive bidding more than doubles target-paper capture and that assigned colluders score target papers about two points higher than honest co-reviewers, while conference-wide effects remain comparatively modest. Evaluated bid-phase detectors provide only limited evidence of collusion: in a fixed-triplet detector stress test, native positive-bid graphs are confounded by benign affinity, while a Very-High-only diagnostic view enables precise but low-coverage local recovery.
